title: Total Time a Reset Timer Runs
statement:
A status light turns on whenever it is triggered and stays on for duration seconds. A trigger at second t keeps the light on from t up to (but not including) t + duration. If the light is triggered again while it is on, the timer restarts from the new trigger; it does not add a second full duration on top.

You get the trigger times times in non-decreasing order and the duration. Return the total number of seconds the light is on.

examples.why: The light is on 2→5 (restarted at 4, so it runs to 7), then 10→13: 5 + 3 = 8 seconds. Adding 3 per trigger would give 9.
The first window ends at 4 exactly when the second starts. They touch but do not overlap, so both count in full.
Three triggers at the same second restart the same window: on from 5 to 7.

hints: Each trigger opens a window [t, t + duration). The answer is the total length covered by the union of these windows.
Because triggers are sorted, a window can only be cut short by the very next trigger.
Trigger i contributes min(duration, times[i + 1] − times[i]); the last trigger contributes the full duration.

explain.intuition:
This is the debounce timer from frontend work: every new event restarts the countdown. Each trigger opens a window [t, t + duration), and the answer is the length of the union of all windows.

Since the triggers are sorted, the only thing that can cut a window short is the next trigger. If the next trigger comes after the window has closed, the window counts in full; otherwise it only counts until the next trigger takes over. So each trigger adds min(duration, next − t), and the last adds the full duration. No interval list is needed.
steps: For each i from 0 to n − 2, add min(duration, times[i + 1] − times[i]).
pitfalls: Adding duration per trigger, which double-counts overlapping windows.
Treating windows that touch (the next trigger at exactly t + duration) as overlapping. The window is half-open, so both count fully.
Using 32-bit arithmetic in languages that have it: the total can reach about 2 · 10<sup>9</sup>.

solutions.title: Merge windows explicitly
solutions.idea: Build each window, extend the current merged window while the next one starts before it ends, and add up merged lengths.

solutions.title: Each trigger until the next one
solutions.idea: A trigger's window is cut short only by the next trigger, so it adds min(duration, gap to the next trigger).

followups: Triggers now add time to the remaining countdown instead of restarting it. How does the total change?
Times arrive unsorted. What is the cost now, and can you avoid a full sort?
